items.title: Wakeful Practice Opens: What Counts as the First Watch and the Last Watch

items.zh: 復次，初夜後夜常勤修習覺寤瑜伽者，云何初夜？云何後夜？云何覺寤瑜伽？云何常勤修習覺寤瑜伽？言初夜者，謂夜四分中，過初一分，是夜初分。言後夜者，謂夜四分中，過後一分，是夜後分。覺
items.en: Within the Basic Section, in the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples, the first yogic process, the Ground of Setting Out Towards Liberation, the third part of the third chapter … Furthermore, as for one who constantly and diligently cultivates wakeful practice in the first watch and the last watch of the night: what is the first watch? What is the last watch? What is wakeful practice? What is constant, diligent cultivation of wakeful practice? The first watch means that, of the night's four divisions, the first division, once reached, is the night's first part. The last watch means that, of the night's four divisions, the last division, once reached, is the night's last part.

items.title: Wakeful Practice Defined: Walking and Sitting Around the Clock

items.zh: 寤瑜伽者，謂如說言：於晝日分經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心。於初夜分經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心、淨修心已，出住處外洗濯其足，還入住處，右脇而臥，重累其足，住光明想、正念、正知、思惟起想巧便而臥。至夜後分，速疾覺寤，經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心。
items.en: Wakeful practice means: it is said that, during the day, one purifies the mind of the obstructions and what accords with them through walking meditation and sitting meditation; in the first watch of the night, one purifies the mind of the obstructions and what accords with them through walking meditation and sitting meditation. Having purified the mind, one goes outside the dwelling to wash the feet, then returns inside, lies down on the right side, one leg resting upon the other, abiding in the perception of light, mindfulness, and clear comprehension, forming the intention to rise, and lying down skilfully. Upon reaching the last watch, one wakes swiftly, and again purifies the mind of the obstructions and what accords with them through walking meditation and sitting meditation.

items.title: Constant Diligent Cultivation: Five Kinds of Energy

items.zh: 常勤修習覺寤瑜伽者，謂如有一世尊弟子，聽聞覺寤瑜伽法已，欲樂修學，便依如是覺寤瑜伽，作如是念：我當成辦佛所聽許覺寤瑜伽。發生樂欲，精進勤劬，超越勇猛勢力發起、勇悍、剛決、不可制伏、策勵其心無間相續。
items.en: As for one who constantly and diligently cultivates wakeful practice: it is like a disciple of the Blessed One who, having heard the teaching on wakeful practice, wishes to study and practice it, and, relying on this wakeful practice, thinks: I shall accomplish the wakeful practice permitted and taught by the Buddha. Such a one generates aspiration, strives with vigour, arises with a force that surpasses ordinary courage, is bold, resolute, unable to be overcome, and spurs the mind on in unbroken continuity.

items.zh: 此中云何於晝日分經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心？

items.title: Walking and Sitting Meditation, in Technical Detail

items.zh: 言晝日者，謂從日出時至日沒時。言經行者，謂於廣長稱其度量一地方所，若往、若來相應身業。言宴坐者，謂如有一，或於大床、或小繩床、或草葉座，結加趺坐，端身正願，安住背念。
items.en: The day means the time from sunrise to sunset. Walking meditation means the bodily act of going and coming within a properly measured stretch of ground, back and forth. Sitting meditation means: it is like one who, on a large bed, a small rope bed, or a seat of grass and leaves, sits cross-legged, holds the body upright, forms a correct resolve, and abides turned away from unwholesome thought.

items.title: Section: The Five Hindrances and Their Five Provoking Conditions

items.zh: 所言障者，謂五種蓋。順障法者，謂能引蓋、隨順蓋法。云何五蓋？謂貪欲蓋、瞋恚蓋、惛沈睡眠蓋、掉舉惡作蓋、及以疑蓋。云何順障法？謂淨妙相，瞋恚相，黑闇相，親屬、國土、不死尋思，追憶昔時笑戲喜樂承事隨念，及以三世或於三世非理法思。
items.en: The obstructions are the five hindrances. What accords with the obstructions is whatever draws out a hindrance or conforms to it. What are the five hindrances? The hindrance of desire, the hindrance of ill-will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, and the hindrance of doubt. What accords with the obstructions? The mark of what is attractive; the mark of resentment; the mark of darkness; preoccupation with kin, homeland, and one's own mortality, together with recollecting past laughter, play, pleasure, and service rendered to elders; and incorrect reflection on the three times.

items.title: Purifying the Mind During Walking Meditation: The Perception of Light

items.zh: 問：於經行時，從幾障法淨修其心？云何從彼淨修其心？答：從惛沈睡眠蓋，及能引惛沈睡眠障法，淨修其心。為除彼故，於光明想善巧精懇，善取善思、善了善達。
items.en: Question: During walking meditation, from how many obstructions is the mind purified, and how is it purified from them? Answer: The mind is purified from the hindrance of sloth and torpor, and from whatever draws out that hindrance. In order to remove it, one becomes skilful and earnest regarding the perception of light — skilfully grasping it, skilfully reflecting on it, skilfully understanding it, and skilfully penetrating it.

items.zh: 以有明俱心，及有光俱心。或於屏處、或於露處往返經行。於經行時，隨緣一種淨妙境界，極善示現，勸導、讚勵、慶慰其心。謂或念佛、或法、或僧、或戒、或捨、或復念天。
items.en: This is done with a mind accompanied by brightness, and a mind accompanied by light. One paces back and forth in walking meditation, whether in a sheltered place or in the open. During walking meditation, taking as object any one pure and excellent condition, one calls it vividly to mind, and thereby exhorts, encourages, and comforts one's own mind — namely, by recollecting the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, moral discipline, generosity, or the divine realms.

items.title: More Antidotes to Drowsiness, and the Formula That Closes Them

items.zh: 或於宣說惛沈睡眠過患相應所有正法，於此法中，為除彼故，以無量門訶責毀呰惛沈睡眠所有過失，以無量門稱揚讚歎惛沈睡眠永斷功德。所謂契經、應頌、記別、諷誦、自說、因緣、譬喻、本事、本生、方廣、希法、及以論議。為除彼故，於此正法聽聞受持，以大音聲若讀、若誦，為他開示，思惟其義，稱量觀察。或觀方隅，或瞻星月諸宿道度，或以冷水洗灑面目。由是惛沈睡眠纏蓋未生不生，已生除遣。如是方便，從順障法淨修其心。
items.en: Or, among the teachings that speak of the faults of sloth and torpor, one dwells on that teaching, and through countless approaches censures and condemns every fault of sloth and torpor, and through countless approaches praises and extols the merit of permanently ending it. …In order to remove it, one hears and retains this teaching, reciting or reading it aloud, explaining it to others, reflecting on its meaning, and weighing and examining it. …Or one gazes at the four directions, or looks up at the stars, moon, and their courses, or washes the face with cold water. By this, the entanglement of sloth and torpor does not arise if not yet arisen, and is removed if already arisen. Such are the skilful means by which the mind is purified of what accords with the obstructions.

items.title: Section: Purifying the Mind During Sitting Meditation — Four Remaining Hindrances

items.zh: 問：於宴坐時，從幾障法淨修其心？云何從彼淨修其心？答：從四障法淨修其心。謂貪欲、瞋恚、掉舉惡作、疑蓋，及能引彼法，淨修其心。為令已生貪欲纏蓋速除遣故，為令未生極遠離故，結加趺坐，端身正願，安住背念。或觀青瘀、或觀膿爛、或觀變壞、或觀膖脹、或觀食噉、或觀血塗、或觀其骨、或觀其鎖、或觀骨鎖，或於隨一賢善定相作意思惟。
items.en: Question: During sitting meditation, from how many obstructions is the mind purified, and how is it purified from them? Answer: The mind is purified from four obstructions — desire, ill-will, restlessness-and-remorse, and doubt — and from whatever draws them out. …In order to swiftly remove the hindrance of desire once arisen, and to keep it far away before it arises, one sits cross-legged, holds the body upright, forms a correct resolve, and abides turned away from unwholesome thought; and one contemplates a corpse turning livid, or festering, or decaying, or bloating, or being devoured, or smeared with blood, or reduced to bones, or reduced to bones held by sinew, or a skeleton of linked bones — or one reflects with the mind fixed on any one excellent, virtuous mark of concentration [within concentration already attained].

items.zh: 或於宣說貪欲過患相應正法，於此法中，為斷貪欲，以無量門訶責毀呰欲貪、欲愛、欲藏、欲護、欲著過失，

blocks.text: Fascicle 24 completes two more provisions: **wakeful practice** (覺寤瑜伽), practising through the first and last watches of the night, and **clear awareness in conduct** (正知而住). Today is a practical guide to walking and sitting meditation and to the hindrances that each counters.

The night has four divisions: the first is the first watch, the middle two the middle watch (for sleep), the last the last watch. Master Cháng Bǎi: if one thinks, "I'll get up at three," the ālayavijñāna records it, and one wakes.

Having heard the teaching on wakeful practice, the disciple resolves to accomplish it, and the treatise piles up terms for that energy: one "generates aspiration, strives with vigour, arises with a force that surpasses ordinary courage, is bold, resolute, unable to be overcome, and spurs the mind on in unbroken continuity". Master Cháng Bǎi: it is like armour; "one going into battle must wear armour so as not to be wounded by arrows."

"Walking meditation means going and coming within a properly measured stretch of ground." Venerable Miào Jìng: walking keeps blood and energy flowing; "if you only sit, they stagnate." Sitting is cross-legged on a seat or bed.
Each hindrance has a "provoking condition": for desire, attractive features; for ill will, irritating ones; for restlessness, recalling past laughter and pleasure (Venerable Miào Jìng); and so on.

Walking meditation counters dullness and drowsiness, with the **perception of light** and the **six recollections**: of the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, moral discipline, generosity, and the gods. Or one looks at the four directions, the stars and moon, or washes the face with cold water.

Sitting counters the other four: desire, ill will, restlessness and remorse, and doubt. Against desire, impurity meditation: the skeleton, in detail or in outline. Venerable Miào Jìng: done here with a concentrated mind, it goes deeper than before.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say "the first watch" is?
options: the last division of the night
of the night's four divisions, the first division is the night's first part
quiz.why: "The first watch means that, of the night's four divisions, the first division passed through is the night's first part." Master Cháng Bǎi: the treatise divides day and night into four periods each, three hours apiece, so the night has twelve hours.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi illustrate "forming the intention to rise"?
options: thinking "I'll get up at three," the storehouse consciousness records it and one wakes at three
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: for example, if one thinks, "I'll get up at three tomorrow," the storehouse consciousness records it, and one wakes at three.

quiz.q: How do the two masters analyse the string "generates aspiration, strives with vigour … bold, resolute, unable to be overcome"?
options: Cháng Bǎi maps it to five kinds of energy, like armour-energy, donning armour for battle; Miào Jìng reads the first part as vow and, from "bold" on, as action
both say they are mere synonyms
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: just as one going into battle must wear armour so as not to be wounded by arrows — this is armour-like energy. Venerable Miào Jìng: what comes before is vow; here it turns to action, and actual action is called "bold."

quiz.q: Why does Venerable Miào Jìng say walking meditation is indispensable?
options: it keeps the blood and energy flowing; sitting constantly lets them stagnate and cause problems
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: walking helps blood and energy flow normally; if you only sit, they stagnate and problems arise — so walking is a must.

quiz.q: Recollecting past laughter, play, and pleasure is the provoking condition for which hindrance, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: restlessness — it is the prelude to restlessness
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: recalling laughter and pleasure is the prelude to restlessness — the condition that accords with that hindrance.

quiz.q: What six recollections does the treatise list for walking meditation, and which Saṅgha does Master Cháng Bǎi say is recollected?
options: the Buddha, Dharma, Saṅgha, discipline, generosity, and the gods; the noble Saṅgha
quiz.why: "Namely, by recollecting the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, moral discipline, generosity, or the divine realms." Master Cháng Bǎi: the Saṅgha recollected is the noble Saṅgha, not ordinary monks.

quiz.q: The text lists gazing at the directions, the stars, and washing with cold water. Citing the Āgamas, what does Master Cháng Bǎi say to do if one is still sleepy after all methods?
options: go to sleep, and when refreshed, get up and continue
quiz.why: "Or one gazes at the four directions, or looks up at the stars, moon, and their courses, or washes the face with cold water." Master Cháng Bǎi: the sutra says that if all eleven methods have been tried and one is still sleepy, one simply goes to sleep, and gets up to continue once refreshed.
